analyticalQuestion: On the frozen R0.73K grid, does the largest Fourier cutoff show a d-uniform discrete viscous branch with the expected first-order drift, controlled projector conditioning, and closed cutoff diagnostics?
supportedTakeaway: At N=160 and epsilon at most 10^-3, every sampled d node retains one numerically real eigenvalue in the fixed circle; the drift quotient approaches the independently derived inviscid-adjoint formula, projector diagnostics remain finite, and adjacent-cutoff discrepancies close to roundoff by N=160.
